title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative: The Ministry of Manpower launched a Guide for labour inspectors in the Palm Oil Sector in early 2022. The guide has been field-tested by labour inspectors at both national and provincial levels. This Guide traces its basis to the extensive discussions in the strategic planning workshop and has been developed to assist labour inspectors to conduct more targeted and relevant investigations of working conditions in the palm oil sector. Establishment of tripartite forum in Bitung for the fishing sector on 4 October 2022. This is a follow-up activity post sectoral strategic planning activities in the first half of 2022. The main purpose of the forum was to raise awareness of compliance with Labour Standards, Occupational Safety and Health, and Gender Equality and the importance of social dialogue and collective bargaining in preventing labour disputes. As part of strategic compliance plans, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) launched NORMA 100 0n 27 June 2023. The NORMA 100 initiative intends to develop a self-assessment tool for companies to monitor their own working conditions (both general working conditions and occupational safety and health). Providing such tools to enterprises can be a useful way for Governments to improve employer awareness of national labour laws and encourage integration of decent work into management practices, particularly when anchored in dialogue between employers and workers. The ILO with US funding has been actively working with the tripartite constituents in Indonesia to promote decent work in the palm oil sector. The focus has been to strengthen the institutional capacity of the tripartite to promote workers’ rights and decent work in the sector. During 2020-2021, the ILO and the Ministry convened a workshop on strategic compliance planning in the palm oil sector. The event brought together the stakeholders from the inspectorate, the employers’ organizations, enterprises, and unions, as well as technical specialists from the ILO, to identify ways to improve workplace compliance and the involvement of the social partners in promoting a culture of compliance. Started in West Kalimantan in 2022 and now The Guide is used by labour inspectors in other provinces such as South Sumatra, Riau, and North Sumatra. US funding facilitated the formation of the tripartite forum. attended by the local governments, and the representatives of employers’ and workers’ organizations in the fish processing sector, the forum resulted in the signing of a joint declaration that outlines three common objectives for all participating agencies/stakeholders which are: 1) to increase productivity and competitiveness of the fish processing sector in North Sulawesi, 2) to improve compliance with labor laws and regulations, and 3) to prevent violence and harassment in the workplace. BWI, the ILO, and Malaysia’s Palm Oil Sector provided inputs and a technical note from ILO to the Ministry on these self-assessments in the context of labour inspection system. The ILO supported consultations with social partners and other relevant government institutions in the development of the tools.

title.narrative: 1.3.2. Number of Member States with targeted strategic compliance plans, developed in consultation with the social partners
Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative:
The Regional Secretary of the Central Java Province issued a new Decree Number 523/012 Year of 2023 Concerning Joint Monitoring Team for Labour Norms on Fisheries Vessels at Fishing Ports within the Jurisdiction of the Central Java Province. Two local government offices in Central Java Province, namely the Local Marine Affairs and Fisheries and Local Manpower and Transmigration Offices of Central Java Province worked together to develop a decree on joint inspection onboard fishing vessels. Coordinating Ministry of the Maritime Affairs and Investment issued a Decree No. 29/2023 concerning Coordination and Harmonisation Team for Laws and Regulations Related to the Protection of Workers in the Fisheries Sector Especially Those Working on Board Fishing Vessels on 23 February 2023. At the national level, Indonesia has many Government Ministries/Institutions involved in fishing sectors. As a result, many laws and regulations in fishing sectorwere issued by various ministries often without proper coordination. Considering this, with the objective to improve the protection of workers working in this sector including those working onboard foreign fishing vessels, the Coordinating Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Investment, worked closely with various relevant ministries to harmonize laws and regulations in Indonesia's fishing sector. With this decree, Indonesia established a team to harmonize laws and regulations in Indonesia's fishing sector which consist of representatives of various relevant Government Ministries/Institutions. The team will organize series of technical coordination meetings to recommend some technical actions to harmonize laws and regulations in Indonesia's fishing sector. The ILO with EU funding supported the development of the local decree, which started from a series of focused group discussions involving the local manpower office and local marine affairs and fisheries office of Central Java Province as well as with the Indonesian Ministry of Manpower and Indonesian Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries. The FGD includes a visit to relevant fishing ports in Central Java Province. The ILO also supported the development of the text of the local decree. After the issuance of the local decree, the ILO supported the initial joint inspection activities including the promotion of labour standards and OSH onboard fishing vessels to workers, fishing owners, and relevant government officials. The ILO with EU funding supported the process to develop the decree for the establishment of the harmonization team. In close collaboration with the Coordinating Ministry, since 2022 the ILO facilitated coordination meetings with various relevant government ministries to get the commitment to work together in a team to harmonize laws and regulations in the fishing sector in Indonesia. The ILO also supported technical meetings to develop the draft of the decree of the establishment of the harmonization team.
Furthermore, the ILO, as requested by the Coordinating Ministry, continues to support the plan to organize a series of technical meetings to develop recommendations for harmonizing laws and regulations in Indonesia's fishing sector.
